name: Bin He
title: Trustee Professor of Biomedical Engineering; Professor of Neuroscience Institute; Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering by courtesy
department: Biomedical Engineering; Neuroscience Institute; Electrical and Computer Engineering by courtesy
fitReason: Strong specialized AI-to-physical-control fit through convolutional EEG decoding, same-day adaptation and human-machine learning. A software/decoding project on existing data could be narrower than participant-facing experiments, but is not an offered short-term project.

physicalEvidence.summary: The complete June 2025 study deploys EEGNet-8.2 convolutional decoding with same-day fine-tuning to control an actual four-finger Allegro Hand. Twenty-one able-bodied participants had prior BCI experience and passed an offline decoding screen; decoded two- or three-finger choices drove visible physical finger movements. This establishes learned robotic execution, not arbitrary dexterous object manipulation or broad clinical effectiveness. Bin He conceived and supervised the study, with his CMU group and students explicitly identified. The distinct July 2026 joint-learning study uses cursor tasks and vibrotactile feedback; it is fresh AI work, not a new physical-hand deployment.

shortVisit.summary: The current lab positions page advertises prospective PhD and postdoctoral research participation. It does not establish an external-master summer 2027 research visit, eight-week project, stipend or remote arrangement.

name: Kathleen Candon
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
researchAreas: Learning from implicit and explicit feedback
fitReason: Highly direct CS/HRI fit in learning reward and preference models from human action choices and evaluative feedback. Her current research identity is independent of her prior Yale advisors; the reviewed physical experiment is attributed to the Yale collaboration rather than claimed as Skidmore infrastructure.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full September 2026 IMPLIED manuscript reports 20 participants collaborating with a real Franka Emika Panda to assemble toy pizzas. A Gaussian-process implication model and preference-weight learning update during interaction and influence ingredient choices; MoveIt Task Constructor handles pick-and-place motion while the Shutter robot provides social cues. The task uses known, discrete high-level actions and stable preferences. This is online learned physical collaboration at Yale, coauthored by Candon, not verified deployment in her new Skidmore lab. The earlier first-authored HRI 2026 PIE study used offline preference estimation, as the newer paper explicitly distinguishes.

The separate institutional scholar process is only a possible administrative inquiry.
